description: Render the WORKFLOW.md prompt template against the normalized issue and attempt. Templates are written in the REQUIRED minimal template subset (Section 5.4): {{ }} interpolation with dotted member access, {% for %}...{% endfor %} iteration over a list and over a map, and indexed access to the two elements of a map entry's key/value pair — the surface every conforming implementation MUST render, and the only surface a vector's template uses. Strict mode: an unknown variable and an unknown filter MUST fail rendering, and Section 5.5 makes the error class a REQUIRED spelling, so the class asserted below is the one a conforming implementation reports. A class names the condition, not the stage that detected it (Section 5.5): an engine that resolves filter names while parsing still reports an unknown filter as template_render_error, and template_parse_error is reported only for a body that is not well-formed template syntax. Templates are single-line and use delimiters rather than inter-token whitespace so the expected output does not depend on an engine's whitespace-control behavior. Section 12.2 also fixes what iterating a nested structure yields: a list yields its elements in list order, and a map yields its entries in ascending order of key, keys compared as strings by Unicode code point, with each entry a two-element key/value pair, key first. That order governs the maps a template names by path (the issue object and metadata) and not a blocker ref's own fields, which Section 12.2 reads by name rather than by iteration. Section 12.2 also fixes what a bound null renders to (the empty string), closes the issue object's member set to Section 4.1.1's fields, and fixes a timestamp's rendering to RFC 3339 in UTC.
given: { template: string, issue: object, attempt: integer | null }
expect: { rendered: string } on success, or { error: string } naming the error class on failure

vectors.description: A known issue field renders as its value.
Several known fields render in place.

expect.rendered: ENG-42: Fix the login bug [In Progress]

vectors.description: A nested list (Section 12.2) can be iterated; delimiters avoid whitespace-control ambiguity.

given.template: {% for l in issue.labels %}[{{ l }}]{% endfor %}

vectors.description: A nested map (Section 12.2) iterates in ascending key order, and an entry is a two-element key/value pair with the key first. The keys are supplied in an order that is not ascending; there are three rather than two because two agree with any order one time in two. The expectation does not depend on the supplied order, so a harness whose JSON decoder reorders object keys still checks the rule.

given.template: {% for kv in issue.metadata %}[{{ kv[0] }}={{ kv[1] }}]{% endfor %}

vectors.description: The issue object is itself a map a template may name whole (Section 12.2), so it iterates in ascending key order too. The expected keys are the fields Section 4.1.1 defines, and the vector rests on those being the normalized record's members: an implementation exposing a template field beyond Section 4.1.1 renders an entry this vector does not expect. The two are held in agreement by scripts/validate_spec_consistency.py, which reads Section 4.1.1's field bullets and compares them against this vector's given and expected keys and against their order, so a field added to the record without being added here is an error rather than a divergence (decision 0154).

given.template: {% for kv in issue %}[{{ kv[0] }}]{% endfor %}

issue.title: Fix the login bug
issue.description: The login form rejects valid credentials.

vectors.description: Ascending is by Unicode code point (Section 12.2), which a locale collation is not. The keys are apple, U+00E5r and U+00E4rlig: by code point U+00E4 precedes U+00E5, so the order is apple, U+00E4rlig, U+00E5r, where an en_US collation gives apple, U+00E5r, U+00E4rlig and a Swedish tailoring gives the same as en_US. The three sort identically precomposed and decomposed, so the vector separates the comparison rather than the normalization form, of which Section 12.2 applies none.

given.template: {% for kv in issue.metadata %}[{{ kv[0] }}]{% endfor %}

vectors.description: The attempt variable renders when present as an integer (retry/continuation run).
Strict mode: a reference to a variable that is neither issue nor attempt MUST fail rendering (Section 5.4).

Strict mode: an unknown filter MUST fail rendering (Section 5.4). The REQUIRED minimal subset defines no filters, so this vector is satisfied by an implementation that offers none as well as by one that offers some and lacks this one (screaming): it asserts the strict-failure rule rather than the absence of a particular filter. The class is template_render_error even where the engine resolves filter names while parsing, because a class names the condition rather than the stage that detected it (Section 5.5).

A body that is not well-formed template syntax is template_parse_error (Section 5.5). This is the iterate-labels template with its closing tag removed, so the only difference from the passing vector is the malformation.

attempt is always bound (Section 12.1); on a first run it is null and renders as the empty string rather than failing rendering (Section 12.2), since strict variable checking is a rule about names the render context does not define and attempt is a name this specification defines.
A bound value that is null renders as the empty string (Section 12.2), here a nullable Section 4.1.1 issue field supplied as null.

The issue object's members are closed to Section 4.1.1's field set (Section 12.2); naming a member outside it fails template_render_error (Section 5.5) rather than rendering as null, which is what keeps the null rule safe for a genuinely absent field. The template names assignee, the singular near-miss of the real field assignees, which is the case a prompt author actually hits rather than an arbitrary unknown name.
A timestamp field (Section 4.1.1) renders as RFC 3339 in UTC (Section 12.2), the form Section 11.3 already parses on the way in.
